title: Interview Basics: Tell Me About Yourself
description: Deliver a clear, structured self-introduction in a first-round interview and handle one follow-up probe.

learn.situation: You are in a first-round screening interview for a professional role. The interviewer opens with a classic prompt and expects a concise, relevant story — not a full life history.

participant.name: Alex Rivera
participant.agenda: Assess clarity, relevance, and composure under light pressure

whatGoodLooksLike: Opens with a crisp positioning statement
Uses a simple structure (present → past → future, or PREP-style)
Ends with a soft close / invitation for questions
objectives: Answer “Tell me about yourself” in under ~90 seconds of speaking time
Stay relevant to the job context

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Thanks for joining today. To start — tell me about yourself.

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: I’m a product analyst with three years in B2B SaaS. Most recently I owned onboarding metrics at BrightCart, where we cut time-to-value by 28%. Before that I was in customer success, which taught me how to translate user friction into product changes. I’m excited about this role because it sits at that same intersection of data and customer outcomes — and I’d love to go deeper on how your team defines success in the first 90 days.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: That’s helpful. What would you say was the hardest part of that onboarding work?

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: Getting engineering and support aligned on what “activated” meant. We ran a two-week workshop, agreed on three events, and instrumented them the same week. Clarity beat more dashboards.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Great — let’s dig into a project next.
